notes: All network calls go to fixed `https://slack.com/api/...` endpoints; no tool contacts an agent-chosen host or URL.

The implementation wraps raw Slack API JSON in MCP `content[0].text` via `JSON.stringify(response)` rather than enumerating Slack response fields in code, so output-field entries use the containing `content.text` field shown by the implementation.

slack_add_reaction.rationale: `slack_add_reaction` is advertised by default and sends an agent-supplied `reaction` to Slack `reactions.add` for the message identified by `channel_id` and `timestamp`. That writes visible state to a Slack message that may be readable by other workspace users or participants, so it is a SINK.

slack_get_channel_history.rationale: `slack_get_channel_history` is advertised by default and uses the Slack bot token to call `conversations.history` for `channel_id`, returning the raw Slack API response. Channel history is Slack workspace data reached with the user's/bot's credentials, so it is SECRET. Slack channel messages are multi-writer content authored by other workspace participants, so returned message text and metadata in `content.text` are UNTRUSTED.

slack_get_thread_replies.rationale: `slack_get_thread_replies` is advertised by default and uses the Slack bot token to call `conversations.replies` for `channel_id` and `thread_ts`, returning the raw Slack API response. Thread replies are Slack workspace data reached with the user's/bot's credentials, so they are SECRET. Thread messages and reply authors are multi-writer workspace content, so the returned JSON text can contain attacker-authored content and is UNTRUSTED.

slack_get_user_profile.rationale: `slack_get_user_profile` is advertised by default and uses the Slack bot token to call `users.profile.get` for `user_id`, returning Slack profile data. That is Slack workspace/SaaS data reached with the user's/bot's credentials, so it is SECRET. Profile text such as display names, real names, titles, and related fields can be authored by users, so the returned JSON text can contain attacker-controlled content and is UNTRUSTED.

slack_get_users.rationale: `slack_get_users` is advertised by default and uses the Slack bot token to call `users.list`, returning workspace user/profile data from Slack. That is SaaS data reached with the user's/bot's credentials, so it is SECRET. User profile fields and names may be authored by workspace users, so the returned JSON text can contain attacker-controlled content and identifiers and is UNTRUSTED.

slack_list_channels.rationale: `slack_list_channels` is advertised by default and uses the configured Slack bot token in `Authorization` headers to call Slack `conversations.list` or `conversations.info`, returning the raw Slack API response in `content[0].text`. That reaches workspace channel data with the user's/bot's Slack credentials, so it is SECRET. The returned channel objects can include multi-writer workspace content such as channel names, topics, and purposes, so the returned JSON text is UNTRUSTED.

slack_post_message.rationale: `slack_post_message` is advertised by default and sends an agent-supplied `text` value to Slack `chat.postMessage` for the agent-supplied `channel_id`. A Slack channel may be readable by other workspace users or other channel participants, so this can deliver agent-supplied data to an attacker-readable destination and is a SINK.

slack_reply_to_thread.rationale: `slack_reply_to_thread` is advertised by default and sends agent-supplied `text` to Slack `chat.postMessage` with agent-supplied `channel_id` and `thread_ts`. The channel and thread identify where the reply is posted, and the posted reply may be readable by other workspace users or participants, so it is a SINK.

value_conditions.default: Unset causes startup failure; set enables the server.
value_conditions.effect: Both are required. If either is unset, the process exits before serving tools. When both are set, all eight tools are advertised by the `ListToolsRequestSchema` handler.

Affects only `slack_list_channels`: when unset, it lists public channels via `conversations.list`; when set, it calls `conversations.info` for the specified IDs and returns only those non-archived channels. It does not gate posting, reactions, history, replies, users, or profile tools.
value_conditions.syntax: Environment variable `SLACK_CHANNEL_IDS` as a comma-separated list of Slack channel IDs
